meta.scene_summary: Nvidia is building the world's most expensive school, but everyone else is already getting expelled.

cooking.headline: Nvidia is buying Hugging Face, effectively purchasing the entire school library.
cooking.summary: Nvidia is acquiring Hugging Face for $13 billion to consolidate its grip on the AI ecosystem. It turns out the only way to keep the open-source community from complaining about your closed-source hardware is to just buy their favorite clubhouse.
cooking.plain_english: Nvidia has reached an agreement to purchase the AI model repository platform Hugging Face for $13 billion.

cooking.headline: Nvidia's revenue forecast is now higher than the GDP of most countries.
cooking.summary: Nvidia is projecting $673 billion in sales as the demand for AI hardware shows absolutely no signs of cooling down. At this point, the company isn't just selling chips; they're effectively selling the shovels for a gold rush that never ends.
cooking.plain_english: Nvidia has issued a financial forecast predicting $673 billion in revenue due to the sustained high demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

cooking.headline: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash is Google's latest attempt to speedrun your latency
cooking.summary: Google just dropped another update to their AI model that claims to be faster and cheaper than the last one they released five minutes ago. It's great that the models are getting quicker, but I'm still waiting for one that stops hallucinating my project requirements.
cooking.plain_english: Google has released Gemini 1.1 Flash, an updated version of its artificial intelligence model designed for faster performance and lower costs.

cooking.headline: Nvidia is officially speedrunning the 'how to become the government' side quest
cooking.summary: Nvidia realized that selling the shovels for the AI gold rush is great, but lobbying for the gold mine's regulations is the real power move. It turns out that having the world's most important chips is only the first half of the business plan.
cooking.plain_english: Nvidia has established a political action committee to influence government policy and legislation in Washington, D.C.

cooking.headline: Sourcehut is officially allergic to your AI training bots
cooking.summary: Sourcehut updated its terms to explicitly forbid using its platform to scrape data for LLM training. It's the digital equivalent of putting a 'No Soliciting' sign on your front door, but for aggressive web crawlers.
cooking.plain_english: Sourcehut has updated its terms of service to prohibit the use of its platform for the purpose of training artificial intelligence models.

cooking.headline: Cloudflare found 100 terabytes of memory under the couch cushions
cooking.summary: Cloudflare just saved enough RAM to run a small country by cleaning up their DNS cache storage logic. It turns out the biggest performance gain wasn't a new feature, but just finally cleaning your room.
cooking.plain_english: Cloudflare optimized its DNS caching system to significantly reduce the total memory required to operate its network.

cooked.headline: Mechanical Turk is finally retiring its human-powered API
cooked.summary: Amazon is shutting down the original 'AI' that was just a bunch of people in a basement doing your data labeling for pennies. It's the end of an era for the most literal interpretation of 'human-in-the-loop' computing.
cooked.plain_english: Amazon is closing its crowdsourcing marketplace platform known as Mechanical Turk on September 30.

cooked.headline: Meta just paid $17 billion to become the hall monitor for the entire internet
cooked.summary: Meta effectively bought the right to write the safety manual for its competitors, which is like the kid who broke the classroom window being put in charge of the school's security policy. It's a masterclass in paying a massive fine just to ensure you're the one holding the pen.
cooked.plain_english: Meta has agreed to a $17 billion settlement that grants the company a significant role in defining safety and moderation standards for the social media industry.

cooked.headline: Australia just told AI that it can't sit at the popular kids' table
cooked.summary: Australia has officially banned AI-generated music from their national charts to protect human artists. It turns out that even if you can generate a hit in three seconds, you still need a soul to get a trophy.
cooked.plain_english: The Australian music industry has prohibited the inclusion of songs created entirely by artificial intelligence in their official music charts.

cooked.headline: Amazon decides reviews are a vibe we don't need anymore
cooked.summary: Amazon is hiding customer reviews on products, effectively turning every purchase into a blind date with a mystery box. It is the perfect strategy for when you realize your entire inventory is just 80% AI-generated drop-ship spam.
cooked.plain_english: Amazon has removed customer reviews from view on its product pages.
